paper_metadata.title: Effect of μ precipitation and γ′ evolution on intra-/intergranular strength of Ni-Co-Cr-based superalloys after 800 ℃ thermal exposure

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: The initiation of microscopic defects and the microstructural stability are crucial factors in determining the tensile strength and failure mechanism of Ni-Co-Cr-based superalloys.

evidence.section: 4. Conclusions
evidence.quote: This study investigated the phase transition and coarsening behavior of the microstructure of Ni-Co-Cr-based superalloys following long-term thermal exposure.

evidence.section: 2. Materials and experiments
evidence.quote: The samples were isothermally exposed at 800 ℃ for 10, 20, 50, 100, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, and 10,000 h.

evidence.section: 3.1. Evolution of the γ′ and μ precipitates in the isothermally exposed
evidence.quote: The microstructure thermally exposed at 800 ℃ consists mainly of a γ matrix, a significant amount of γ ′ precipitates, a smaller quantity of μ phases, and some carbides.

evidence.section: 3.1. Evolution of the γ′ and μ precipitates in the isothermally exposed

evidence.section: results and discussion
evidence.quote: Intragranular γ′ typically undergoes coarsening during elevated temperature thermal exposure, which is characterized by a stable volume fraction, increased phase-interface distance, and decreased quantity.

evidence.section: results and discussion
evidence.quote: The μ phase precipitates in the samples analyzed in this study were predominantly observed at the GBs, particularly near large intergranular γ′ precipitates, which may be due to the segregation of Co, Cr, Mo, and W associated with the intergranular γ/γ′ phase.

evidence.section: 3.2. μ precipitates around the large intergranular γ′ phase

evidence.section: results and discussion
evidence.quote: Dislocation shearing is the primary deformation mechanism in intragranular γ′ precipitates during high-temperature tensile deformation, and involves numerous slip lines, SFs, and nanotwins (Fig. 8 (b)).

mechanisms.name: crack initiation at μ phase interface

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: Cracks tended to nucleate preferentially at the μ phase interface during high-temperature tensile testing, leading to the breakage of the γ / γ ′ precipitates and formation of pores owing to crack propagation.

evidence.section: 3.4. Effect of the μ and γ′ phases on inter/intragranular defects
evidence.quote: This behavior can be attributed to the brittleness of the μ phase, which leads to stress concentration at the matrix interface.

evidence.section: 3.4. Effect of the μ and γ′ phases on inter/intragranular defects
evidence.quote: The nucleation and growth of the μ phase consumes a significant amount of refractory elements, such as W and Mo, weakening the solid solution strength of the alloy.

evidence.section: results and discussion
evidence.quote: the enrichment of refractory elements in the μ precipitates reduces the solid solution-strengthening effect in the γ matrix surrounding the μ precipitates [29,30].
